item.content:encoded:
The Centre for Global Child Health (CGCH) at The Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids) in Toronto, Canada, is inviting applications for the Global Child Health (GCH) Fellowship Program. This prestigious fellowship is designed for professionals who are passionate about improving child health outcomes around the world through research, leadership, innovation, and capacity building.

The fellowship offers an outstanding opportunity for individuals from diverse healthcare and research backgrounds to develop the skills needed to become leaders in global child health. Participants will work alongside internationally recognized researchers and practitioners while contributing to projects that address some of the world’s most pressing child health challenges.

About the Global Child Health Fellowship Program

The Global Child Health Fellowship Program is a comprehensive two-year interdisciplinary training program that prepares fellows for impactful careers in global health.

Rather than focusing solely on academic learning, the program combines practical experience with leadership development. Fellows become actively involved in the design, implementation, analysis, and evaluation of research and capacity-building initiatives that improve health systems and child well-being worldwide.

Hosted by the Centre for Global Child Health at SickKids, one of the world’s leading pediatric hospitals, the fellowship provides an exceptional learning environment where fellows collaborate with experts addressing complex global health issues.

Fellowship Objectives

The program aims to prepare the next generation of global health leaders by helping fellows:

  • Build advanced leadership skills.
  •  Strengthen research capacity.
  •  Develop expertise in implementation science.
  •  Improve project management and evaluation skills.
  • Contribute to innovative global health initiatives.
  •  Support health system strengthening in low- and middle-income countries.
  • Enhance collaboration across multidisciplinary teams.

Research Areas

Fellows may contribute to projects covering a wide range of global child health topics, including:

  • Nutrition
  • Child growth and development
  •  Pediatric oncology
  •  Infectious diseases
  • Climate change and child health
  • Microbiome research
  • Vaccine development
  •  Complex systems and network science
  • Implementation science
  • Health systems strengthening
  • Health workforce training
  • Capacity building initiatives
  • Other emerging global health priorities

This broad range of research themes allows fellows to gain practical experience while addressing real-world health challenges affecting children globally.

Fellowship Duration

The fellowship runs for two years .

During this period, fellows will participate in interdisciplinary research, leadership training, scholarly development, and collaborative projects under the mentorship of experienced global health professionals.

Who Can Apply For This Fellowship  Opportunity?

The fellowship welcomes applicants from a wide variety of educational and professional backgrounds.

Eligible applicants may include professionals in fields such as:

  • Medicine (MD)
  •  Doctoral graduates (PhD)
  •  Nursing
  • Allied Health Professions
  • Public Health
  •  Health Research
  •  Other relevant healthcare disciplines

Individuals with a strong commitment to improving child health through research, education, implementation science, or capacity building are encouraged to apply.

Why Apply?

Participating in the Global Child Health Fellowship Program provides numerous professional and academic benefits, including:

  • Training at one of Canada’s leading pediatric research institutions.
  • Mentorship from internationally recognized global health experts.
  •  Leadership development opportunities.
  • Hands-on experience in global health research.
  • Exposure to interdisciplinary collaborations.
  •  Opportunities to contribute to high-impact projects.
  • Professional networking with researchers and health professionals from around the world.
  • Preparation for long-term careers in global health research and policy.

Application Process

Interested applicants should review the official fellowship information and complete the online application before the deadline.

Applicants are encouraged to prepare all required documents well in advance to avoid last-minute delays.

Application Portal

Apply for this opportunity HERE

Important Dates

 Application Deadline :  September 13, 2026 (11:59 p.m. EDT)
Expected Fellowship Start: On or before July 2, 2027

Contact

Applicants with questions regarding the fellowship may contact the Global Child Health Fellowship Program Committee through the official contact information provided by SickKids.

Conclusion

The Global Child Health Fellowship Program at SickKids offers an exceptional opportunity for healthcare professionals and researchers seeking to make a meaningful impact on child health worldwide. Through world-class mentorship, interdisciplinary collaboration, leadership training, and involvement in transformative research projects, fellows will gain the expertise needed to address global child health challenges.

If you aspire to become a leader in global health research or capacity building, this fellowship represents an excellent pathway toward achieving that goal. Interested applicants should submit their applications before September 13, 2026, to be considered for this highly competitive program.

Discover more fellowship opportunities like this on the OFY webpage .

item.content:encoded:
Young African professionals interested in public health, digital health, research, and healthcare innovation are invited to join the Africa CDC Youth Public Health & Digital Health Research Training Workshop 2026, a three-day virtual hands-on training taking place from 27–29 July 2026.

The training will bring together 100 young professionals from across Africa to strengthen their practical skills in research design, research methodology, and concept note development.

Key Details

Program: Public Health & Digital Health Research Training Workshop 2026
Dates: 27–29 July 2026
Duration: 3 days
Format: Virtual
Participants: 100 young professionals from across Africa
Eligibility: Exclusively for members of the Africa Youths in Digital Health Network (YiDHN)
Focus Areas: Research design, research methodology, and concept note development
Collaboration: West African Institute of Public Health
Network: Africa Youths in Digital Health Network (YiDHN), an initiative under the Africa CDC Youth Program
Join YiDHN: https://bit.ly/join_yidhn

About the Africa CDC Youth Public Health & Digital Health Research Training Workshop 2026

The Public Health & Digital Health Research Training Workshop 2026 is designed to equip young African professionals with practical skills to strengthen their capacity to conduct research and contribute to innovation in public and digital health.

Taking place virtually from 27 to 29 July 2026, the three-day hands-on workshop will provide participants with practical knowledge in research design, research methodology, and the development of strong concept notes.

Organized in collaboration with the West African Institute of Public Health, the training will bring together 100 young professionals from across Africa, creating an opportunity to build research capacity, foster collaboration, and advance digital health innovation across the continent.

What Will Participants Learn?

The training will focus on three core areas:

  • Research Design: Strengthening participants’ ability to develop structured and relevant research approaches.
  • Research Methodology: Building practical knowledge of methods and approaches for conducting effective research.
  • Concept Note Development: Developing the skills needed to prepare clear and compelling research concept notes.

Participants will also have the opportunity to connect with other young professionals interested in public health, digital health, research, technology, and healthcare innovation across Africa.

Who Can Participate?

The Public Health & Digital Health Research Training Workshop is exclusively for members of the Africa Youths in Digital Health Network (YiDHN).

The workshop will accommodate 100 young professionals from across Africa who are interested in strengthening their research capacity and contributing to digital health innovation.

Those who are not yet members of YiDHN can join the network through the onboarding form.

About the Africa Youths in Digital Health Network (YiDHN)

The Africa Youths in Digital Health Network (YiDHN) is an initiative under the Africa CDC Youth Program aimed at empowering young professionals across Africa to lead the transformation of healthcare through digital solutions.

The network brings together young people passionate about digital health and provides opportunities to connect, build capacity, collaborate, and contribute to shaping the future of healthcare in Africa.

Through the network, young professionals can also gain access to future training, mentorship, networking, and capacity-building opportunities.

Why Join the YiDHN?

Africa’s rapidly evolving digital health landscape creates significant opportunities for young professionals to contribute to healthcare transformation through research, technology, innovation, and collaboration.

By joining YiDHN, young professionals can become part of a growing continental network focused on fostering innovation, building capacity, and driving impactful change in digital health across Africa.

Membership also provides an avenue to learn about opportunities such as the Public Health & Digital Health Research Training Workshop and future initiatives for young digital health professionals.

How to Join the Africa Youths in Digital Health Network

Interested young professionals can complete the Africa Youths in Digital Health Network (YiDHN) Onboarding Form to join the network.

Join the YiDHN here:
https://bit.ly/join_yidhn

Join a community of young African professionals working to advance digital health innovation, research, capacity building, and healthcare transformation across Africa.

item.content:encoded:
The World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) is offering a Fellowship opportunity with the WIPO Knowledge Center (WKC) in Geneva, Switzerland. The fellowship has a contract duration of 12 months, with the possibility to renew, and provides a monthly stipend of CHF 6,000.

Key Details

Organization: World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO)

 Eligibility: Open to applicants worldwide who meet the requirements.
Fellowship: Fellowship – 26229-FEL
Section: WIPO Knowledge Center, IP Futures and Knowledge Management Section, Administration, Finance and Management Sector
Duty Station: CH-Geneva
Location: WIPO Headquarters, Geneva, Switzerland
Contract Duration: 12 months
Stipend: CHF 6,000 monthly
Anticipated Start Date: October 1, 2026
Publication Date: 22-Jul-2026
Application Deadline: 06-Aug-2026, 10:59:00 PM
Grade: N/A

IMPORTANT NOTICE REGARDING APPLICATION DEADLINE: Please note that the deadline for applications is indicated in local time as per the time zone of the applicant’s location.

 

1. Organizational context

(a) Organizational Setting

The World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) is a United Nations specialized agency. Its WIPO Knowledge Center (WKC) is the custodian of the knowledge repository, which is an authoritative source for global IP academic research. The WKC oversees WIPO’s physical and digital library collection, in addition to the dissemination of WIPO publications.

The WKC team requires a qualified Fellow to support the library and knowledge services by collecting, analyzing, and reporting data that informs evidence-based decision-making. Working closely with colleagues, the fellow will contribute to the assessment of library services, digital resources, and user engagement, helping to identify opportunities to improve discoverability, accessibility, and service delivery.

Fellowships aim to provide fellows with experience to strengthen their knowledge and professional competence, which they can apply in their professional field once they have completed their fellowship with WIPO.

(b) Reporting Lines

The Fellow shall work under the supervision of the Head of the WIPO Knowledge Center (WKC).

(c) Objectives

During the fellowship, the Fellow will assist with the WKC activities and gain in-depth knowledge and competence in the respective field.

2. Duties and responsibilities

The Fellow will provide support in the following areas:

a) Collect, validate, and manage quantitative and qualitative data relating to library services, digital collections, and information resources.

b) Gather, monitor, and analyze usage statistics from library platforms, repositories, websites, and other digital services.

c) Produce regular statistical reports to support strategic planning and operational decision-making.

d) Analyze trends in resource usage, identifying patterns and opportunities for improvement.

e) Assist in developing and maintaining key performance indicators (KPIs) for library services and digital initiatives.

f) Contribute to the evaluation of digital resources, collections, and services using evidence-based assessment techniques.

g) Assist in collecting and analyzing citation, bibliometric, altmetric, and other research impact data, where applicable.

f) Prepare reports, presentations, and briefing materials summarizing analytical findings for internal stakeholders.

h) Collaborate with colleagues to improve workflows for data collection, reporting, and assessment.

i) Perform other related duties as required.

3. Requirements

(a) Education

Essential:

At least a first-level degree in library, information science, knowledge management or a related field. Recognized professional qualification.

(b) Experience

Essential:

At least two years of professional experience working in a library, knowledge management, research support, or related environment.

Experience collecting, managing, and analyzing library or information-related data.

Experience working with usage statistics, service metrics, or other performance data to support assessment activities.

Experience preparing analytical reports and presenting findings to support decision-making.

Experience using spreadsheet software and data analysis tools.

Desirable:

Experience working with integrated library systems, institutional repositories, discovery platforms, or digital library services.

Experience using business intelligence, dashboard, or data visualization tools.

Experience working with bibliometric, altmetric, or research impact indicators.

Experience with SQL, Python, R, or other analytical tools would be an advantage.

(c) Languages

Essential: Excellent (written and spoken) knowledge of English.

Desirable: Good knowledge of at least one of WIPO’s other official languages would be an advantage.

(d) Specific skills and competencies

Essential:

  • Sound understanding of library operations and digital information services.
  • Knowledge of library assessment methodologies and performance measurement.
  • Ability to collect, clean, organize, and interpret data from multiple sources.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with excellent attention to detail.
  • Ability to identify trends and communicate findings clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Good understanding of statistical concepts and data visualization principles.
  • Ability to work independently while contributing effectively within a collaborative team.
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills.

4. Organizational competencies

  1. Communicating effectively.
  2. Showing team spirit.
  3. Demonstrating integrity.
  4. Valuing diversity.
  5. Producing results.
  6. Showing service orientation.
  7. Seeing the big picture.
  8. Seeking change and innovation.
  9. Developing yourself and others.

5. Terms and conditions

a) Term of fellowship: A fellowship may be granted for a period of up to 12 months with the possibility to renew.

b) Anticipated Start Date: October 1, 2026.

c) Location: WIPO Headquarters, Geneva, Switzerland.

d) Stipend: CHF 6,000 monthly.

e) Travel expenses: WIPO shall contribute towards the cost of the fellow’s travel on engagement and separation from service. If necessary, WIPO may provide assistance in obtaining an entry visa to Switzerland.

f) WIPO contributes towards the medical insurance and provides accident insurance coverage during the course of the fellowship.

g) WIPO will request a “carte de legitimation” for the Fellow, which serves as a residence and work permit, from the Permanent Mission of Switzerland to the United Nations Office and to the other international organizations in Geneva. Family members of the Fellow are not eligible for a “carte de legitimation.”

h) Tax and social security: Fellows shall be solely responsible for meeting any taxation and social security obligations that may arise directly or indirectly from their contract with WIPO.

FOR MORE INFO AND TO APPLY NOW CLICK HERE

Additional information

WIPO values diversity among its personnel and is committed to equal employment opportunities. We welcome applications from qualified candidates from unrepresented Member States of WIPO, and from underrepresented geographical regions and groups, including people with disabilities. If candidates need any accommodation to participate in the recruitment process, they should contact their HR focal point when they receive an invitation.

Fellows are not staff members of WIPO, and the position does not lead to any employment rights and entitlements beyond the terms of the fellowship.

The Fellowship will take place in Geneva, Switzerland and it cannot be carried out remotely.

By completing an application, candidates understand that any willful misrepresentation made on this web site, or on any other documents submitted to WIPO during the application, may result in disqualification from the recruitment process, or termination of employment with WIPO at a later date, if that employment resulted from such willful misrepresentations.

In the event that your candidature is shortlisted, you will be required to provide, in advance, a scanned copy of an identification and of the degree(s)/diploma(s)/certificate(s) required for this position. WIPO only considers higher educational qualifications obtained from an institution accredited/recognized in the World Higher Education Database (WHED), a list updated by the International Association of Universities (IAU) / United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). The list can be accessed through the link: http://www.whed.net/. Some professional certificates may not appear in the WHED and these will be reviewed individually.

Additional testing/interviewing may be used as a form of screening. Initial appointment is subject to satisfactory professional references.

FOR MORE INFO AND TO APPLY NOW CLICK HERE

item.content:encoded:
OVERVIEW

In 2023, the CVF-V20 and the Boston University Global Development Policy Center launched the V20 Climate Prosperity Fellowship Program for finance officials (or equivalent) from CVF-V20 Member Countries. The Fellowship Program is an integral part of the CVF-V20’s ongoing efforts to promote and drive ambitious climate action and to mobilize international support for climate vulnerable nations.

The aim of the V20 Climate Prosperity Fellowship Program is to engender cooperation among CVF-V20 member states, provide them with the tools to combat challenges they may face in the pursuit of strategies to avert climate breakdown, and pioneer the development of economic and financial solutions, including the mobilization of domestic climate finance towards positive climate action.

The V20 Climate Prosperity Fellowship Program is designed to provide mid- to senior career officials with opportunities for peer-learning, building cutting-edge technical skills to integrate climate change into their work, and supporting their leadership in advancing innovative solutions. The CVF-V20 has consistently emphasized the need to reform the international financial architecture to unlock opportunities on the ground to promote climate prosperity. Through weekly webinars, interactions with experts, residencies, and immersive exercises, V20 Climate Prosperity Fellows will have a unique opportunity to work together in advancing a fit for purpose international financial architecture.

COLLABORATION OBJECTIVES

At the end of the program, Fellows are expected to be well positioned to support resource mobilization for Climate Prosperity Plans and to:

  • Understand the international financial architecture and be able to identify opportunities to support climate prosperity;
  • Engage in policy discussions concerning reform of the international financial architecture;
  • Harness the knowledge and skills needed to engage and access processes associated with the international financial architecture, including on debt reform, shifting of financial flows, carbon financing exchanges, and mainstream surveillance of climate risks to drive new investment;
  • Identify and deploy communications strategies used to raise awareness of the priorities of the climate-vulnerable countries in relation to the reform of the international financial architecture; and
  • Contribute to the formulation and implementation of their countries’ Climate Prosperity Plans.

TARGET OUTCOME

To provide peer-learning and technical enhancement support to the finance ministries (or equivalent) of 16 to 20 CVF-V20 member countries by equipping Fellows with skills to pursue the mobilization of financial resources more effectively to support ambitious national climate prosperity plans for development positive climate action.

KEY ACTIVITIES

  • Participation in online classes/seminars/workshops;
  • Participation in one-week in-person residencies in January 2027 and October 2027;
  • Participation in relevant meetings, supported by the CVF-V20;
  • Participation in interactive discussions with representatives of International Financial Institutions and partner groups with the support of the CVF-V20; and
  • Preparation and delivery of presentations during V20 Senior Officials Meetings and relevant CVF-V20 workshops and events.

CONDITIONS OF PARTICIPATION

Candidates from Ministries of Finance (or equivalent) in CVF-V20 member countries who meet the requirements set out below are invited to apply to participate in the year-long Fellowship Program for the period 2026- 2027:

  • Citizen of a CVF-V20 member country;
  • Official with demonstrated five to ten years of mid- to senior-level experience in international affairs, public policy and/or development, including climate/environmental/sustainable development;
  • Committed to participate in the Fellowship program’s activities organized throughout the year, both online and in-person and to complete and submit assignments as required;
  • Willingness to travel abroad to attend in person meetings and training sessions with members of their cohort;
  • Commitment to attend scheduled weekly virtual sessions for the duration of the fellowship period;
  • Committed to working and sharing information with their national government and national stakeholders after the completion of the Fellowship;
  • Committed to integrating into the growing network of V20 CPP fellows and staying engaged in the community to advance common priorities and mutual learning; and
  • Proﬁcient in English.

*Prospective Fellows interested in undertaking intensive training in debt sustainability analyses should indicate the same in their application and, in so doing, commit to an additional session to undertake this training each week. Proficiency in using Microsoft Excel and familiarity with macroeconomic concepts are recommended.

APPLICATION PROCESS

Interested officials must submit their application by accomplishing the form:

Submit your application here

The deadline for submission of applications is on 31 July 2026.

TENTATIVE FELLOWSHIP TIMELINE

Month
August 2026
Selection and notification of Fellows
September 2026
Finance Ministries (or equivalent) provide official confirmation of selected Fellows’ participation in the Program
October 2026
Weekly webinars begin and continue throughout the year
January 2027

First in-person residency
*Location will be confirmed in due course
January 2027
Proposals for capstone projects submitted for feedback
March 2027
Fellows provide inputs to the V20 Senior Officials Meeting
March 2027

Virtual Meeting

Fellows contribute to preparations for the Spring Meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank Group, including through the identification of priorities, policy goals, and strategies with the goal to put together a singular document for Spring Meetings priorities, with the possibility of sharing externally, as well as to the V20 Communiqué.
April 2027

2027 Spring Meetings of the IMF and the World Bank Group

Fellows contribute to the hybrid sessions on topics relevant to the CVF-V20

Virtual or in-person participation during the 18th V20 Ministerial Dialogue
October 2027

Second in-person residency
*Location will be confirmed in due course

Presentation of final capstone projects

Conclusion of the program and graduation

item.content:encoded:
The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Ethiopia has announced a Call for Proposals for Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) and NGOs under the Spotlight Initiative Africa Regional Programme (SIARP) 2.0 to End Violence Against Women and Girls (EVAWG).

This opportunity invites eligible civil society organizations to submit proposals to contribute to efforts aimed at ending violence against women and girls across Africa. The initiative provides an opportunity for organizations working on gender equality, women’s rights, prevention of gender-based violence, advocacy, community engagement, and related areas to participate in a major regional programme.

Applications must be submitted through the UNDP Quantum Supplier Portal by 29 July 2026 at 4:00 AM New York time.

About the UNDP Call for Proposals

The call is managed by UNDP Ethiopia and relates to the Spotlight Initiative Africa Regional Programme (SIARP) 2.0 to End Violence Against Women and Girls (EVAWG).

The programme seeks to support efforts to address violence against women and girls through collaboration with civil society organizations and other partners.

Opportunity at a Glance

Organization: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)

Office: UNDP Ethiopia

Programme: Spotlight Initiative Africa Regional Programme (SIARP) 2.0

Focus: Ending Violence Against Women and Girls (EVAWG)

Contract Type: Civil Society Organizations (CSOs)

Duty Station: Home-based

Programme Duration: August 2026 – December 2028

Expected Start Date: Upon signing of the agreement

Application Deadline: 29 July 2026 at 4:00 AM New York time

Reference Number: UNDP-ETH-00754

Contact: info.procurementet@undp.org

Who Can Apply?

The call is specifically targeted at Civil Society Organizations (CSOs).

Organizations interested in applying should carefully review the official solicitation and negotiation documents available through the UNDP Quantum Supplier Portal to determine the full eligibility, technical, administrative, and documentation requirements.

Applicants should ensure that the organization name entered during supplier registration is the full legal name corresponding with the organization’s legal and bank account records.

About the Spotlight Initiative Africa Regional Programme 2.0

The services under this call relate to the Spotlight Initiative Africa Regional Programme (SIARP) 2.0 to End Violence Against Women and Girls (EVAWG).

The programme focuses on efforts to address violence against women and girls in Africa and strengthen action toward gender equality and women’s rights.

Civil society organizations have an important role in this work, including through community engagement, advocacy, prevention, service delivery, accountability, and advancing the rights and agency of women and girls.

Applicants should consult the official tender documents for the precise scope of work, expected results, deliverables, eligibility criteria, and proposal requirements.

Contract Duration and Location

The assignment is expected to run from August 2026 through December 2028, with the agreement commencing upon signing.

The duty station is listed as home-based, making this a particularly relevant opportunity for qualifying organizations capable of contributing to the programme’s regional objectives without being based at a UNDP office.

How to Apply for the UNDP CSO Call for Proposals

Applications must be submitted electronically through the UNDP Quantum Supplier Portal.

Interested organizations should:

  1. Register on the UNDP Quantum Supplier Portal if they do not already have a supplier profile.
  2. If already registered, log in using the existing supplier account. Do not create another profile.
  3. Search for the negotiation using reference number UNDP-ETH-00754.
  4. Subscribe to the tender to receive notifications about amendments or updates.
  5. Create a draft response in the system to indicate your intention to submit a proposal. This enables UNDP to send relevant notifications if the tender requirements are amended.
  6. Review all negotiation and solicitation documents carefully before preparing the application.
  7. Submit the complete offer directly through the Quantum Supplier Portal before the deadline.

Organizations that have previously registered but cannot remember their login details should use the forgotten password/username functionality rather than creating a new account.

Questions or requests for clarification should be submitted using the messaging functionality available within the procurement system, in accordance with the solicitation instructions.

Important Information for Applicants

When registering in the supplier portal, applicants should enter the organization’s full legal name exactly as it appears in its legal and bank account documentation.

Organizations should also subscribe to the tender after locating it in Quantum. This is important because UNDP may issue amendments, clarifications, or updates before the submission deadline.

Interested CSOs are strongly encouraged to begin the registration and application process early to allow sufficient time to review the solicitation documents and resolve any supplier portal issues.

Application Deadline

The deadline for submissions is:

29 July 2026 at 4:00 AM (New York time).

Applications must be submitted directly through the UNDP Quantum Supplier Portal in accordance with the requirements of the solicitation.

Given the deadline, prospective applicants should review the opportunity and begin preparing their submissions as soon as possible.

Official Application and Further Information

Tender Reference: UNDP-ETH-00754

Application Portal: UNDP Quantum Supplier Portal

UNDP Resources for Bidders: Applicants can consult UNDP’s procurement resources for guidance on supplier registration, using the Quantum system, and submitting bids.

Procurement Office: UNDP Ethiopia Procurement Unit

Contact Email: info.procurementet@undp.org

Applicants should rely on the official UNDP procurement notice and solicitation documents for the definitive eligibility criteria, requirements, deadlines, and application instructions.

 

APPLY NOW

item.content:encoded:
The Roosevelt Institute is inviting experienced policy professionals, researchers, academics, and experts to apply for the Good Life Residents Program 2026, a prestigious six-month remote residency designed to cultivate innovative policy leaders and generate transformative ideas that advance economic justice in the United States.

As part of the Roosevelt Institute’s broader Good Life Agenda, selected residents will work alongside leading economists, policy experts, researchers, and senior advisors to develop original policy proposals addressing some of the country’s most pressing economic challenges. Participants will produce policy essays, collaborate with subject matter experts, contribute to national policy conversations, and receive $3,000 in compensation, along with travel and accommodation support for the program’s concluding event if required.

One of the featured residency tracks is the AI and Finance Residents Program, created in partnership with Data & Society, which focuses on examining how artificial intelligence is transforming finance, investment, labor markets, industrial policy, and the broader economy.

This residency provides an outstanding opportunity for experienced professionals who are passionate about shaping public policy, promoting equitable economic growth, and influencing the future of AI governance.

About the Roosevelt Institute Good Life Residents Program

The Good Life Residents Program is a six-month policy residency that brings together a small cohort of emerging and established policy thinkers to explore solutions aligned with the Roosevelt Institute’s vision for a stronger and more equitable economy.

Rather than conducting traditional academic research, residents focus on producing practical, people-centered policy ideas that can influence public debate and policymaking.

The program emphasizes collaboration, mentorship, public engagement, and intellectual exchange.

Throughout the residency, participants work closely with:

  • Roosevelt Institute Think Tank directors
  • Senior organizational leadership
  • Topic advisors
  • Fellow residents
  • Policy practitioners
  • Academic experts
  • Organizers and government leaders

Each residency concludes with a public event designed to amplify participants’ ideas and encourage dialogue on important national and state-level policy issues.

AI and Finance Residents Program

One of the Roosevelt Institute’s featured residency topics explores the rapidly evolving relationship between artificial intelligence and finance.

Massive investments in generative AI have significantly reshaped the economy, influencing:

  • Stock markets
  • Financial markets
  • Corporate profits
  • Bond issuance
  • Employment trends
  • Industrial development
  • Trade policy
  • Technology investment
  • Economic growth

Today, just seven technology companies account for more than one-third of the total market capitalization of the S&P 500, raising concerns about market concentration, financial stability, and economic inequality.

The Roosevelt Institute, together with Data & Society, seeks residents capable of producing bold policy ideas that help redirect AI investment toward broader public benefit while protecting workers, strengthening democratic institutions, and encouraging sustainable innovation.

Objectives of the AI and Finance Residency

The residency seeks to answer important policy questions such as:

  • How can governments better oversee private AI investments?
  • How can policymakers reduce excessive concentration within the technology sector?
  • How can AI investment benefit society rather than only large corporations?
  • How can governments encourage investment across other important sectors of the economy?
  • How should AI policy balance innovation, public safety, labor protections, and national competitiveness?
  • What democratic institutions are needed to ensure accountability over public investments in AI?
  • How can governments support technology research that strengthens supply chains and sustainability?

Participants are encouraged to propose original, practical, and people-centered policy recommendations.

What Residents Will Do

Successful applicants will participate in numerous activities throughout the six-month residency.

These include:

Develop Original Policy Essays

Residents will research and write an approximately 1,500-word policy essay presenting innovative solutions aligned with the Roosevelt Institute’s Good Life Agenda.

Each essay responds to a specific policy prompt within the resident’s assigned topic area.

Join a Small Collaborative Cohort

Each topic area consists of only three to four residents, creating an environment that encourages meaningful collaboration, peer learning, and intellectual exchange.

Residents will work closely with one another throughout the program.

Work with Expert Advisors

Every cohort is supported by one or two Topic Advisors.

These advisors include:

  • Leading academics
  • Government practitioners
  • Policy leaders
  • Organizers
  • Industry experts

They provide:

  • Intellectual mentorship
  • Strategic guidance
  • Feedback on policy proposals
  • Moderation during discussions and public events

Participate in Public Events

At the end of the residency, participants present and discuss their policy ideas during a public event organized by the Roosevelt Institute.

The event helps amplify participants’ work while encouraging national dialogue around economic policy.

Contribute to Public Engagement

Residents may also participate in:

  • Opinion editorials (Op-Eds)
  • Press interviews
  • Reporter briefings
  • Public policy discussions
  • Media engagement opportunities

Serve as Good Life Agenda Ambassadors

Participants are expected to promote and represent the Roosevelt Institute’s Good Life Agenda throughout their professional and public networks.

Program Structure

Each residency topic includes:

  • 3–4 Good Life Residents
  • 1–2 senior Topic Advisors
  • Roosevelt Institute policy staff
  • Organizational leadership support

The program emphasizes mentorship, collaboration, and practical policy development.

Program Duration

The residency lasts:

  • Six months

Time Commitment

Residents should expect to dedicate approximately:

  • 5–8 hours per month

This makes the residency suitable for professionals balancing existing work or academic responsibilities.

Location

The program is primarily:

  • Remote

However, participants may be invited to travel for selected meetings or the final public event.

Compensation

Selected residents will receive:

  • $3,000 stipend
  • Travel expenses covered (if required)
  • Accommodation for the concluding event (if required)

This financial support enables participants to fully engage in the residency while contributing meaningful policy work.

Who Should Apply?

The Roosevelt Institute encourages applications from individuals with substantial experience in policy development, technology, economics, or related fields.

Ideal applicants include:

  • Policy professionals
  • Researchers
  • Economists
  • Academics
  • Government practitioners
  • Technology policy experts
  • AI researchers
  • Industrial policy specialists
  • Think tank professionals

Candidates should demonstrate both subject expertise and a commitment to developing policies that improve economic outcomes for society.

Required Qualifications

Successful applicants should have:

  • Demonstrated expertise in artificial intelligence, technology policy, industrial policy, or a related discipline.
  • A minimum of five years of professional or academic policy experience.
  • Strong analytical and writing abilities.
  • An interest in advancing equitable economic policy.
  • The ability to collaborate within multidisciplinary teams.
  • A commitment to contributing original policy ideas.

Benefits of Joining the Program

Participants will enjoy numerous professional benefits, including:

  • $3,000 financial compensation.
  • National exposure through public events.
  • Collaboration with leading policy experts.
  • Individual mentorship from senior advisors.
  • Opportunity to publish original policy work.
  • Professional networking opportunities.
  • Media and press engagement.
  • Flexible remote participation.
  • Travel and accommodation support for program events.
  • Contribution to shaping future AI and economic policy discussions.

Why This Residency Matters

Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming economies worldwide.

While AI offers tremendous opportunities for innovation and productivity, it also presents challenges related to wealth concentration, labor markets, financial stability, public accountability, and democratic governance.

The Roosevelt Institute’s Good Life Residents Program seeks individuals capable of proposing practical policy solutions that ensure AI serves broader public interests rather than reinforcing existing inequalities.

Participants have the opportunity to contribute directly to one of today’s most important public policy conversations while helping shape future economic policy.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should visit the Roosevelt Institute’s official Good Life Residents Program webpage and complete the online application according to the published application instructions.

Applicants should carefully review all eligibility requirements before submitting their materials.

APPLY NOW

Application Deadline

Please read and complete this application by the end of the day on Wednesday, August 12, 2026, to be considered for the Good Life Residents Program on AI, presented by the Roosevelt Institute and Data & Society.

Reach out to rooseveltsociety@rooseveltinstitute.org with any questions or concerns.

Program Term: 6 months (September–February 2027)
Time Commitment: Part-Time (~5–8 hours/month)
Location: Remote; Travel may be requested for select convenings

Conclusion

The Roosevelt Institute Good Life Residents Program 2026 offers an exceptional opportunity for experienced policy professionals and researchers to shape conversations around artificial intelligence, finance, and economic justice. Through expert mentorship, collaborative research, public engagement, and a funded six-month residency, participants can develop innovative policy ideas capable of influencing national discussions and future policymaking.

For individuals passionate about AI governance, economic equity, and public policy, this residency provides a unique platform to contribute meaningful solutions while expanding professional networks and gaining national visibility.

Visit the OFY website for more Fellowship Opportunities.

The post Roosevelt Institute Good Life Residents Program 2026: Fully Funded Remote Fellowship Offering $3,000 Stipend for Emerging Economic Policy Leaders appeared first on Opportunities for Youth.

item.content:encoded:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming societies, economies, governments, and public services. As governments increasingly integrate AI into policymaking and service delivery, there is a growing need for innovative civic leaders who can develop responsible, equitable, and community-centered AI policy solutions.

To help address this challenge, the Aspen Policy Academy has launched applications for the AI Civic Action Accelerator 2026, a free virtual accelerator program designed for individuals and small teams seeking to develop impactful AI policy initiatives that strengthen the relationship between governments, communities, and artificial intelligence.

This unique accelerator combines policy education, expert mentorship, peer collaboration, and practical project development to help participants transform promising ideas into actionable policy solutions capable of creating real public impact.

If you are passionate about civic technology, responsible AI governance, public policy, or community innovation, this program offers an exceptional opportunity to refine your ideas and present them directly to policymakers.

About the AI Civic Action Accelerator

The AI Civic Action Accelerator is a free six-session virtual accelerator created by Aspen Policy Academy.

The accelerator is specifically designed for early-stage civic AI policy projects that seek to improve how governments, communities, and artificial intelligence interact.

Rather than focusing on building AI products, the program emphasizes developing policy solutions that help governments respond to emerging AI challenges while ensuring AI serves the public interest.

Participants receive structured guidance to refine their ideas, strengthen their policy proposals, and develop practical advocacy strategies capable of influencing local or state-level decision-making.

The accelerator is ideal for applicants who already have a promising idea but need support turning it into an effective, evidence-based policy initiative.

Program Objectives

The AI Civic Action Accelerator aims to help participants:

  • Develop practical civic AI policy solutions.
  • Learn a proven framework for influencing public policy.
  • Receive personalized feedback from experienced instructors.
  • Collaborate with peers working on similar civic challenges.
  • Build an implementation strategy for policy change.
  • Produce tangible policy outputs.
  • Present solutions directly to policymakers.

Rather than simply teaching policy theory, the accelerator focuses on helping participants produce work that can be implemented in real communities.

Areas of Interest

The Aspen Policy Academy is looking for innovative policy ideas addressing civic AI challenges such as:

Improving Civic Participation

Projects may explore ways AI can:

  • Improve public consultation
  • Increase citizen engagement
  • Enhance democratic participation
  • Make government communication more accessible

Youth Online Safety

Applicants may propose policy solutions that:

  • Protect young people online
  • Improve digital literacy
  • Address AI-generated misinformation
  • Promote safer online environments

Transparent Government AI

Potential ideas include:

  • Responsible AI use within government
  • Transparent decision-making
  • Ethical AI governance
  • Accountability frameworks
  • Fair AI implementation

Workforce and Employment

Applicants may also propose solutions that address:

  • AI automation
  • Workforce transitions
  • Job displacement
  • Government workforce policies
  • Future-of-work planning

Other Civic AI Challenges

The accelerator welcomes creative policy ideas that strengthen relationships between:

  • Governments
  • Communities
  • Artificial intelligence

What Participants Will Learn

Throughout the six-session accelerator, participants will learn Aspen Policy Academy’s proven framework for creating policy impact.

Key learning areas include:

1. Problem Scoping

Participants learn how to:

  • Clearly define policy problems
  • Identify underlying causes
  • Narrow broad issues into actionable challenges

2. Stakeholder Analysis

Participants identify:

  • Government agencies
  • Community organizations
  • Decision-makers
  • Partners
  • Opponents
  • Beneficiaries

3. Policy Alternatives

Participants evaluate:

  • Existing policy approaches
  • Alternative interventions
  • Policy feasibility
  • Practical implementation options

4. Developing Policy Outputs

Participants create practical deliverables that may include:

  • Policy briefs
  • Strategy documents
  • Advocacy materials
  • Community engagement plans
  • Implementation roadmaps

5. Advocacy Planning

The program teaches participants how to:

  • Engage policymakers
  • Build public support
  • Present evidence effectively
  • Develop advocacy campaigns

6. Policy Pitching

The accelerator concludes with participants presenting their refined policy solutions directly to a real decision-maker.

Program Structure

The accelerator consists of:

  • Six live virtual sessions
  • Two hours per session
  • Interactive instruction
  • Hands-on workshops
  • Peer collaboration
  • Individual project development
  • Assignments between sessions
  • Guided readings

Each session combines classroom learning with practical workshopping.

Participants continuously refine their projects based on instructor and peer feedback.

Program Schedule

The accelerator will be conducted virtually over six Thursdays.

Session Dates

  • October 22
  • October 29
  • November 5
  • November 12
  • November 19
  • December 3

Time

  • 9:30 AM – 11:30 AM Pacific Time (PT)
  • 12:30 PM – 2:30 PM Eastern Time (ET)

What Participants Will Achieve

By the end of the accelerator, participants will have:

  • A fully refined civic AI policy solution
  • Policy implementation strategy
  • Advocacy roadmap
  • Tangible policy deliverables
  • Experience presenting to policymakers
  • A stronger understanding of policy impact
  • A completion badge upon successful graduation

Attendance Expectations

Successful participants are expected to:

  • Attend all six virtual sessions
  • Complete required assignments
  • Participate in workshops
  • Complete assigned readings

The attendance policy allows participants to miss no more than two hours of programming to remain eligible for graduation and receive a completion badge.

Who Should Apply?

The AI Civic Action Accelerator is intended for individuals and teams who have already developed an early-stage civic AI policy idea but require guidance to strengthen it.

Applicants might still need assistance with:

  • Refining their concept
  • Assessing feasibility
  • Identifying stakeholders
  • Developing policy engagement strategies
  • Building advocacy plans

Examples of Ideal Applicants

Examples include:

  • AI engineers
  • Technology professionals
  • Tech startup founders
  • AI policy communicators
  • Technology lawyers
  • Civic innovators
  • Community advocates
  • Local organizers
  • Public-interest technology professionals
  • Residents seeking AI policy improvements within their municipalities

Who May Not Benefit Most?

The accelerator is designed as an introductory program.

Applicants with substantial policy experience—such as those who have previously worked in professional policy roles or hold a Master’s degree in Public Policy—are likely to be beyond the intended experience level.

Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must satisfy all eligibility criteria.

They must:

  • Be at least 21 years old by the start of the program.
  • Be fluent in English.
  • Live in the United States or be U.S. citizens or permanent residents living abroad.
  • Apply individually or as part of a team of up to four members.
  • Submit only one application per team.

Team Applications

Applicants may apply:

  • Individually
  • As teams of up to four members

Only one application is required per team.

Applicants must provide contact information for every team member during the application process.

Application Timeline

Applications Open

July 16 – September 1, 2026

Interview Period

Selected applicants may be invited for interviews in mid-September 2026.

Admission Notifications

Successful applicants will be informed in late September 2026.

Program Delivery

October 22 – December 3, 2026

APPLY HERE

Application Deadlines

Applicants have two submission opportunities:

Priority Deadline

Tuesday, August 25, 2026, at 11:59 PM Pacific Time

Final Deadline

Tuesday, September 1, 2026, at 11:59 PM Pacific Time

Applicants are encouraged to apply before the priority deadline to maximize consideration.

Why You Should Apply

Participants will benefit from:

  • A completely free policy accelerator
  • Expert instruction from Aspen Policy Academy
  • Direct mentorship
  • Practical policy training
  • Peer collaboration
  • Real-world policy development experience
  • Opportunities to engage decision-makers
  • Enhanced advocacy skills
  • Tangible project outputs
  • Completion badge
  • Valuable professional networking opportunities

Visit HERE to learn more about the AI Civic Action Accelerator 2026

Conclusion

The Aspen Policy Academy AI Civic Action Accelerator offers an exceptional opportunity for aspiring civic innovators, AI professionals, community advocates, and technology leaders to transform promising ideas into impactful public policy solutions. Through expert instruction, collaborative workshops, and direct engagement with policymakers, participants will gain the knowledge, tools, and confidence needed to advance responsible AI governance at the local and state levels.

If you have an innovative civic AI policy idea and want to create meaningful public impact, this free accelerator provides an outstanding platform to refine your proposal, strengthen your advocacy skills, and contribute to the future of ethical and community-centered artificial intelligence.

Application Deadline: Tuesday, September 1, 2026, at 11:59 PM Pacific Time (Final Deadline).

For more global Training opportunities, visit OFY HERE

The post AI Civic Action Accelerator 2026: Apply for the Free Aspen Policy Academy Program to Develop Civic AI Policy Solutions in the United States appeared first on Opportunities for Youth.

item.content:encoded:
Caritas Europa is inviting applications for the position of Policy and Advocacy Officer (Socio-Economic Policy) at its Secretariat in Brussels, Belgium. This is an exciting full-time permanent opportunity for professionals passionate about social justice, poverty eradication, human rights, and influencing European public policy.

The successful candidate will become part of one of Europe’s leading humanitarian and social justice networks, contributing to policy development and advocacy initiatives that seek to build a more inclusive, equitable, and sustainable Europe. Working within the Policy and Advocacy Unit, the officer will help shape policies on socio-economic development, migration, asylum, integration, and social inclusion while collaborating with Caritas member organizations across Europe.

If you have experience in public policy, advocacy, European affairs, human rights, or social policy and are looking to work in an international, multicultural environment, this opportunity could be an excellent next step in your career.

About Caritas Europa

Caritas Europa is a Catholic network comprising 49 member organizations operating in 46 European countries. The organization works with people from all faiths and backgrounds to combat poverty, promote social justice, and protect the dignity of every individual.

It forms one of the seven regional organizations of Caritas Internationalis, a worldwide confederation with more than 160 national member organizations, making it the world’s second-largest humanitarian organization.

Caritas Europa works directly within communities, responding to emergencies while advocating for long-term policy reforms that address the root causes of poverty, inequality, discrimination, and exclusion. The organization strongly believes that people and the environment should always come before profit when shaping public policies.

Position Overview

Position: Policy and Advocacy Officer (Socio-Economic Policy)

Employment Type: Full-time

Contract Type: Permanent

Location: Brussels, Belgium

Department: Policy and Advocacy Unit

Reports to: Policy and Advocacy Director

Starting Date: As soon as possible

The successful candidate will contribute to implementing the Caritas Europa Strategic Framework 2021–2028, annual work plans, and the organization’s Policy and Advocacy Strategy.

The role primarily focuses on:

  • Social and economic policy
  • Poverty eradication
  • Social inclusion
  • Recognition of non-profit social services
  • Migration policy
  • Asylum policy
  • Integration policy
  • Human rights advocacy

Main Objectives of the Role

The Policy and Advocacy Officer will help deliver two major strategic objectives within Caritas Europa’s Strategic Framework.

Strategic Objective 3.1

Influence European social and economic policies to:

  • Eradicate poverty
  • Reduce inequality
  • End social exclusion
  • Improve participation
  • Promote fair socio-economic systems
  • Strengthen social justice

Strategic Objective 3.2

Influence migration, asylum, and integration policies to ensure:

  • Respect for human rights
  • Protection of human dignity
  • Better integration of migrants
  • Inclusive communities
  • Support for families on the move

Key Responsibilities

The successful candidate will undertake a broad range of policy, advocacy, communication, and coordination responsibilities.

1. Policy Development and Monitoring

Responsibilities include:

  • Monitoring EU policy developments
  • Tracking legislation
  • Following Council of Europe policy processes
  • Reviewing consultations
  • Conducting policy analysis
  • Preparing advocacy recommendations
  • Supporting policy implementation

2. Advocacy

The officer will:

  • Develop advocacy strategies
  • Participate in advocacy meetings
  • Prepare policy positions
  • Engage policymakers
  • Represent Caritas Europa
  • Promote organizational priorities

3. Communication

Communication duties include:

  • Writing policy articles
  • Producing advocacy materials
  • Creating social media content
  • Supporting awareness campaigns
  • Promoting Caritas Europa’s policy messages
  • Organizing public events

4. Network Coordination

The role requires close collaboration with Caritas member organizations by:

  • Supporting working groups
  • Coordinating task forces
  • Strengthening communities of practice
  • Facilitating collaboration
  • Enhancing European and national advocacy links

5. Internal Collaboration

The Policy and Advocacy Officer will also:

  • Share information across teams
  • Prepare reports
  • Participate in internal meetings
  • Coordinate with colleagues
  • Ensure consistency across policy work

6. External Representation

When delegated by the Policy and Advocacy Director, the officer will:

  • Attend conferences
  • Participate in policy forums
  • Join advocacy coalitions
  • Engage with media
  • Represent Caritas Europa in public events

Required Qualifications

Applicants should possess either:

  • A Bachelor’s degree, or
  • A Master’s degree

in one of the following fields:

  • Social Policy
  • Economics
  • Law
  • Public Affairs
  • European Studies
  • Human Rights

Equivalent professional experience may also be considered.

Required Knowledge and Technical Skills

Successful applicants should demonstrate knowledge and experience in several areas.

These include:

  • European Union institutions
  • Council of Europe institutions
  • European policy-making processes
  • Legislative monitoring
  • Policy analysis
  • Advocacy methodologies
  • Strategic communication
  • Public awareness campaigns
  • Negotiation
  • Consensus building
  • Stakeholder engagement
  • Project management
  • Event coordination
  • Human rights policy
  • Employment policy
  • Social justice
  • Poverty reduction
  • Social inclusion
  • Integration policy
  • Catholic Social Teaching

Communication Skills

Applicants should possess:

  • Excellent written English
  • Excellent spoken English
  • Strong public speaking skills
  • Facilitation skills
  • Moderation skills
  • Ability to write:
    • Policy papers
    • Briefing notes
    • Position papers
  • Ability to communicate complex policy issues clearly

Knowledge of additional European languages is considered an advantage.

Partnership and Networking Skills

The ideal candidate should have experience working with:

  • Civil society organizations
  • Government institutions
  • European institutions
  • Donors
  • International partners
  • Membership organizations

Applicants should also have experience working within multicultural and international environments.

Personal Attributes

Caritas Europa is looking for candidates who demonstrate:

  • Integrity
  • Professionalism
  • Strong ethical standards
  • Commitment to social justice
  • Respect for confidentiality
  • Teamwork
  • Strong interpersonal skills
  • Initiative
  • Creativity
  • Organizational ability
  • Flexibility
  • Resourcefulness
  • Ability to work under pressure
  • Results-oriented mindset
  • Willingness to travel across Europe
  • Good Microsoft 365 skills
  • Experience with online collaboration platforms

Salary and Employment Benefits

Caritas Europa offers a competitive Belgian employment package.

Starting monthly salaries include:

  • €3,541 for approximately two years of relevant experience
  • €3,814 for approximately five years of relevant experience
  • €4,211 for approximately ten years of relevant experience

Additional employment benefits include:

  • Permanent employment contract
  • 13th salary
  • 14th salary
  • Hospitalization insurance
  • Pension insurance
  • Lunch vouchers
  • Public transport contribution
  • Flexible working arrangements
  • Additional holidays
  • International working environment
  • Opportunities for professional development
  • Regular travel across Europe

Please note that staff members are expected to be based in Belgium.

Diversity and Equal Opportunity

Caritas Europa is committed to:

  • Equal opportunity employment
  • Diversity and inclusion
  • Non-discrimination
  • Safe recruitment
  • Safeguarding vulnerable people

Applications are welcomed from candidates of all backgrounds and communities.

Recruitment Process

The recruitment process includes:

  1. Online application submission
  2. Shortlisting
  3. First-round interviews
  4. Second-round interviews
  5. Written assignment in English
  6. Final selection

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Applicants should also note that Caritas Europa:

  • Does not use AI to screen applications.
  • Expects applicants to complete every stage of the recruitment process authentically without AI assistance.
  • Requires successful candidates to sign the organization’s Code of Conduct.

Application Deadline

Application Deadline: 20 August 2026 (23:59 CEST)

Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications before the deadline.

How to Apply

Interested candidates should complete the online application through the official Caritas Europa recruitment portal before the application deadline.

Applicants should not include a photograph in their application documents.

APPLY HERE

Why This Opportunity Matters

Working as a Policy and Advocacy Officer at Caritas Europa provides a unique opportunity to influence European policies affecting millions of people. The role combines research, advocacy, communication, networking, and international collaboration, allowing professionals to contribute directly to tackling poverty, promoting equality, advancing human rights, and strengthening inclusive societies across Europe.

Professionals passionate about policy change, social justice, and humanitarian values will find this position both impactful and rewarding.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Caritas Europa Policy and Advocacy Officer (Socio-Economic Policy) Job 2026 in Brussels, Belgium

Conclusion

The Caritas Europa Policy and Advocacy Officer (Socio-Economic Policy) position is an outstanding career opportunity for professionals seeking to make a meaningful contribution to European social policy and advocacy. Offering a permanent contract, competitive salary, comprehensive benefits, and the chance to work within one of the world’s largest humanitarian networks, the role provides both professional growth and the opportunity to influence policies that improve the lives of vulnerable communities across Europe. Interested candidates should prepare a strong application and submit it before 20 August 2026 to be considered for this prestigious position.

For more global job opportunities visit OFY HERE

item.content:encoded:
If you are passionate about public service, community development, education, environmental sustainability, youth empowerment, emergency preparedness, nonprofit leadership, or civic engagement, the NYC Service AmeriCorps Program offers an exceptional opportunity to gain meaningful professional experience while making a lasting impact across New York City.

NYC Service AmeriCorps is inviting applications for a wide range of service positions hosted by New York City agencies and nonprofit organizations. Members will work directly with communities, support public initiatives, strengthen nonprofit organizations, and help address some of New York City’s most pressing social, economic, environmental, and educational challenges.

The current recruitment cycle includes 125 available opportunities across numerous organizations and impact areas, allowing applicants to choose roles that align with their interests, skills, and career aspirations. Applicants may select up to three positions during the application process.

About NYC Service AmeriCorps

NYC Service AmeriCorps is designed to help individuals build careers through public service while supporting communities throughout New York City’s five boroughs.

Members serve with either:

  • New York City government agencies
  • Nonprofit organizations

The program combines professional development with community impact by placing participants in organizations working on issues such as:

  • Education
  • Environmental conservation
  • Public health
  • Community outreach
  • Youth development
  • Workforce development
  • Food security
  • Climate resilience
  • Arts and culture
  • Emergency management
  • Volunteer engagement
  • Civic participation
  • Immigrant support
  • Housing
  • Transportation
  • Public policy

The program encourages participants to “Serve Your City, Shape Your Future” by gaining real-world experience while helping solve local challenges.

Why You Should Apply

Serving with NYC Service AmeriCorps provides more than volunteer experience. It offers practical exposure to public administration, nonprofit management, community engagement, and civic leadership.

Participants will have opportunities to:

  • Gain real-world professional experience
  • Serve with respected city agencies and nonprofit organizations
  • Build leadership and communication skills
  • Expand professional networks
  • Strengthen project management abilities
  • Develop community engagement experience
  • Support meaningful public initiatives
  • Build experience for future careers in government, nonprofits, education, public policy, and social impact

Available Opportunity Areas

Applicants can apply for positions in several service tracks, including:

1. Community Outreach Member

Members help organizations strengthen relationships with local communities by:

  • Conducting outreach campaigns
  • Building community partnerships
  • Supporting public education initiatives
  • Promoting public services
  • Organizing community events
  • Expanding volunteer engagement

These positions are available with both nonprofit organizations and New York City agencies.

2. Program Development Member

These positions focus on improving programs through:

  • Research
  • Data analysis
  • Curriculum development
  • Program evaluation
  • Capacity building
  • Strategic planning
  • Community partnerships
  • Policy support

Members contribute to strengthening organizational effectiveness while gaining analytical and administrative experience.

3. Volunteer Management Member

Volunteer Management Members help organizations expand and strengthen volunteer programs by:

  • Recruiting volunteers
  • Coordinating volunteer activities
  • Training volunteers
  • Managing community partnerships
  • Supporting volunteer retention
  • Building sustainable engagement systems

Organizations Participating

The program includes opportunities with numerous respected organizations, including:

  • NYC Department of Transportation (DOT)
  • NYC Parks
  • Department of Sanitation (DSNY)
  • Administration for Children’s Services (ACS)
  • Mayor’s Office of Immigrant Affairs (MOIA)
  • Mayor’s Office of Contract Services (MOCS)
  • NYC Emergency Management (NYCEM)
  • Department of Cultural Affairs (DCLA)
  • Big Brothers Big Sisters of NYC
  • Catholic Charities Community Services
  • Brooklyn Workforce Innovations
  • Queens Public Library
  • Waterfront Alliance
  • RETI Center
  • Counseling in Schools
  • YWCA of the City of New York
  • South Bronx United
  • NYC Public Schools

..…and many other city agencies and nonprofit organizations.

Service Locations

Positions are available throughout New York City’s five boroughs:

  • Manhattan
  • Brooklyn
  • Queens
  • Bronx
  • Staten Island

Each opportunity specifies its borough and host organization.

Language Skills

Some positions welcome or prefer additional language proficiency, including:

  • Spanish
  • Mandarin
  • Cantonese
  • Arabic
  • Haitian Creole
  • Bengali
  • French
  • Urdu
  • Hindi

Language requirements vary depending on the position.

Additional Requirements

Certain host organizations require additional screening, which may include:

  • Background checks
  • Fingerprinting
  • Reference checks
  • Toxicology screening

Applicants should review the individual position descriptions before applying.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should:

  1. Visit the NYC Service AmeriCorps application portal.
  2. Browse the available opportunities.
  3. Use filters to identify positions matching their interests, skills, borough preference, language abilities, and organization type.
  4. Select up to three preferred positions.
  5. Submit the application through the online system.

APPLY HERE

 

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

How many positions are currently available?

The current recruitment cycle lists 125 opportunities across city agencies and nonprofit organizations.

How many positions can I apply for?

Applicants may select up to three positions during the application process.

Where will members serve?

Members serve with nonprofit organizations or New York City government agencies located across the five boroughs.

Are language skills required?

Some positions require or prefer additional language skills, while many are open to English-speaking applicants. Requirements depend on the host organization.

Will every position require a background check?

No. However, several host organizations specify additional screening requirements such as fingerprinting, background checks, or reference verification. Applicants should consult the relevant position description.

Is there an application deadline?

The source material does not specify an application deadline. Applicants are encouraged to apply as soon as possible while positions remain available.

Why This Opportunity Stands Out

NYC Service AmeriCorps offers an excellent pathway for individuals seeking to build careers in public service while directly contributing to communities across New York City. With opportunities spanning education, environmental sustainability, public health, workforce development, emergency management, arts, youth services, immigrant support, and civic engagement, participants can gain valuable experience that strengthens both their professional skills and their commitment to community service.

Click HERE to learn more about the NYC Service AmeriCorps 2026–2027 Applications.

Conclusion

The NYC Service AmeriCorps Program provides a unique opportunity to combine professional growth with meaningful public service. Through placements with city agencies and nonprofit organizations across New York City’s five boroughs, members gain hands-on experience while helping address important community needs.

Whether your interests lie in community outreach, program development, volunteer management, environmental sustainability, education, or public policy, the program offers a diverse range of roles to match your skills and aspirations. Since the source does not indicate a closing date, interested applicants should explore the available opportunities and submit their applications as early as possible.
